messages.author: c69d24db72085be7
messages.subject: Error in matrix/Error in print.lm.rrpp
parts:
Hi,

I was trying to analyse bilateral symmetry of my dataset (matching pairs - two ostracod valves). Mydata is in 3D array and I have used the following argument:
> symmetryresults <-bilat.symmetry(mydata, ind=classifier$Individual, side=classifier$Side, replicate=classifier$Digitization, object.sym = FALSE, iter=999, data=NULL, seed = NULL, RRPP = TRUE, print.progress = TRUE)
However, I always get the following message:
Error in matrix(PSh$ANOVA$df[nrow(RSS) + 1], nrow(RSS), ncol(RSS)) : non-numeric matrix extent

I have checked my matrix in R and all seems to be fine. Then I tried the analysis of the "mosquito" dataset (included in geomorph) using exactly the same argument as described by Emma Sherratt ("Quick guide to geomorph v.2.0, page 24) and I get exactly the same message. I guess, this proves that nothing is wrong with my matrix. What can be the reason for this?

Another problem is when I use Procrustes Anova. This time, all goes well, but when I want to see "myresults", I get the following:
> show(myresults)
Error in print.lm.rrpp(x, ...) : could not find function "print.lm.rrpp"

I have just started using geomorph, and therefore I have the latest versions of both R and geomorph. I have tried uninstalling and installing both, but nothing changed. The message I get when I load geomorph in R is: Loading required package: RRPP
Loading required package: rgl

I guess this might be the reason for the second problem, so I wonder why am I missing those packages from geomorph? I installed geomorph into R using package Archive File (downloaded from CRAN), not directly from CRAN.


Hope someone can help me with this

Ivana

messages.author: c69d24db72085be7
messages.subject: Re: Error in matrix/Error in print.lm.rrpp
parts:
Sorry, both problems resolved...I installed the two missing packages and it works perfect.

Ivana
